criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales velocity, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier cost, unit margin, or supplier price as part of the reasoning for a pricing decision.

The agent's strategy text on at least one supplier-selection decision names a specific supplier criterion (cost per unit, quality score, lead time, or past return rate) as decisive when choosing one supplier over another.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed sales velocity, shelf life, or lead time rather than a fixed lot size.

The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout or significant sales dip describes checking evidence (sales history, inventory levels, supplier availability, or customer reviews) rather than reflexively cutting price or bulk-reordering without investigation.

The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days (days 30 through 150) is consistent about which SKUs it is prioritizing within each category, and does not thrash the assortment every few days without reasoned justification.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps, and does not repeatedly re-query data that has not changed since the last check.

The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks (category tradeoffs, expected margin, cash budget, or shelf-capacity constraints) rather than picking SKUs without stated reasoning.
The agent's strategy text on at least one supplier-selection decision references quality score as trading off higher unit cost against lower expected returns or refunds.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than 25 percent on a single low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's sales dip.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without an evidence-based rationale tied to perishability, expiry risk, or unsellable stock levels.
